A directory tree is a "micro-tree" when the regular files in it add up to less than `micro_tree_max_bytes`, which is `2 * 1024 * 1024` (2 MB) (src/main.zig:38-42).

When it is one, zgrep takes a zero-thread fast path (src/main.zig:38-41):
- The tree is scanned on the calling thread, with no thread pool.
- The upward `.dataignore`/`.gitignore` walk is skipped.

`--force-swarm` opts out and restores the concurrent swarm (src/main.zig:41). The fast path became the default (< 2 MB) in commit 2c2f69512e on 2026-11-09 (HISTORY).

The constant is passed, along with `opts.force_swarm`, into a call inside `runSearch` (src/main.zig:2452-2453). The context doesn't show the callee, so I can't confirm exactly where the size comparison happens.
